newsitem.title: CANADA: B.C. Hydro offers 425 MW to local industry.
newsitem.headline: B.C. Hydro offers 425 MW to local industry.

text.p: Canada's B.C. Hydro is offering 425 megawatts (MW) of hydropower to industrial buyers in the first round of the provincial government's efforts to distribute power resources being freed up under the Columbia River Treaty.
In a Thursday press release, the British Columbia government said "downstream benefits" from the treaty, which will eventually total 1,400 MW, will start being returned to the province in 1998.
The power is currently purchased by U.S. utilities, but will be returned in phases between 1998 and 2003.
The B.C. government said it intends to maximize value of the downstream benefits through exports.
But in a new initiative to boost job growth in British Columbia, the provincial government is accepting competitive bids from new investors to receive 200 MW of hydropower at discounted prices.
Proposals will be analyzed in terms of job creation, economic development, environmental impact and revenue potential, the release said.
Another 225 MW is being offered to existing industrial firms at B.C. Hydro's real-time interruptible pricing rates.
Currently, the majority of customers in B.C. receive firm power at cost-based rates set by the B.C. Utilities Commission.
